text.p: Intimate Brands Inc and its parent, Limited Inc, ended Thursday with lower stock prices after Intimate Brands cautioned that its earnings will be higher than last year's but less than analysts expected.
Limited said it owns about 83 percent of Intimate Brands.
Limited shares closed off 2-1/8 at 18. Intimate Brands ended off 3-1/2 at 16-1/2 after falling more than 4 earlier.
McDonald & Co analyst Jeff Stein said the company wanted to scale back analysts' expectations. Lazard Freres analyst Todd Slater said the forecast is conservative but realistic.
Limited operates 3,949 stores including Lerner and Lane Bryant apparel stores.
Last year, the Limited spun off part of its Intimate Brands division, which includes Victoria's Secret lingerie and Bath & Body Works personal-care items stores. Intimate Brands has 1,588 stores.

In a statement, Intimate Brands said it expects this year's earnings per share to grow about 20 percent and sees at least 16 percent profit growth next year, reflecting anticipated flat sales in the Victoria's Secret catalog unit.
McDonald & Co's Stein said soft catalog sales and slowing second-half sales at Bath & Body Works, which faces increasing competition, are factors.

"Their Victoria's Secret catalog business has had disappointing sales this year," predominantly in apparel which comprises about two-thirds of catalog sales, he said. Catalog operating earnings will likely decline about five to 10 percent next year, Stein said.
But Slater said even with soft sales that business remains more profitable than other catalog companies. It represented only one-tenth of last year's operating earnings, he said.
In other segments, Victoria's Secret stores are doing well and Bath & Body Works has corrected inventory problems, he said.
Slater said he continues to rate the stock a buy. "I have confidence the stock will recover by the end of the year," he said, adding he thought the market overreacted Thursday.

Stein, however, said he thought Thursday's price drop for Intimate Brands makes the stock appropriately valued, saying he believes 15-1/2 is "an attractive entry point." He said he expects it to stay in the 16-18 range while investors wait to see how the Christmas selling season goes.
First Call said analysts expected $1.10 per share earnings in the year ending January, and $1.36 next year compared with $0.85 last year.
Leslie Wexner, who is chairman and chief executive officer of both Limited and Intimate Brands, said in the statement that Intimate Brands is pleased with its performance.

"We've effectively managed tremendous growth at Bath & Body Works," he said. "(We've) built a new store organization at Victoria's Bath & Fragrance and maintained an industry leading profit rate at Victoria's Secret Catalog in the face of a lackluster catalog business environment."
Despite a separate statement that its earnings will be better than expected, Limited stock was off because much of the value of its stock is Intimate Brands, Stein said.
Limited said it expects third quarter earnings to be about $40 million, or $0.15 a share. First Call said analysts had expected $0.13 versus $0.10 a year ago.

NatWest Securities analyst Bob Buchanan said several retailing stocks were off on Thursday. He attributed it to investor concern about 1997 retailer momentum after what is projected to be a decent Christmas holiday selling season.

He said he believes a rally in retailers' share prices under way since February will wind down. Overcapacity and slow demand have had a negative impact on retailer stock prices for three or four years and "I don't see either one of those problems going away," he said.
